correctness.rationale: The LCF period-three adjacency constructs the unique 24-vertex McGee seven-cage. Two standalone independently coded certificates exhaust all 24+276+2024 candidates of cardinality at most three, establishing no smaller solution and exactly 576 successful triples. Both independently build 576-state jump and slide graphs and perform exact all-sources shortest paths or bitset frontier expansions, evaluating all 165600 unordered pairs. They agree on 6184 versus 1328 edges, jump radius/diameter 4, slide radius 8/diameter 9, slide eccentricity counts 432 and 144, locality-penalty histogram and eight exceptional pairs at (jump,slide)=(1,8). A finite exhaustive algorithm is sufficient here because all finite input objects and transitions are explicit, with no pruning or partial sampling.

value.rationale: The 24-vertex McGee graph is the unique smallest cubic graph of girth seven, a canonical benchmark rather than an arbitrary induced subgraph. Exact power-domination configurations model minimal monitoring, and edge-constrained token slides model movement between feasible minimal monitoring states. Eight direct unrestricted sensor changes require eight local slides, forming a disjoint exceptional matching and exhibiting a seven-step penalty not explained by mere connectedness. The exhaustive full pair metric, optimizer enumerator and independent checks give a meaningful reproducible constrained-reconfiguration benchmark. No infinite-family claim is required for this natural exact finite invariant.
